2608.14074.title: Mandato: Protocol-Level Enforcement of Digitally Signed Mandates on AI Agent Actions with Cryptographically Chained Audit Trails
2608.14074.paper_summary: AI agents increasingly act on external systems through standardized tool-calling protocols such as the Model Context Protocol (MCP), yet no infrastructure layer constrains their actions to what a principal has verifiably authorized: authorization logic lives in application code, is neither signed nor independently auditable, and the resulting logs lack evidentiary value. We present Mandato, a governance proxy that enforces digitally signed mandates on agent actions at the protocol level. A mandate is a machine-readable, cryptographically signed authorization artifact specifying which tools an agent may invoke, under which parameter constraints and contextual conditions, for how long, and on whose behalf; the proxy evaluates every tool call against the applicable mandate chain, blocks non-conforming calls in line, and records every decision -- permit, deny, and the evidence for each -- in an append-only, hash-chained audit log designed for evidentiary use and periodically anchored via qualified timestamps. The mandate is deliberately modeled on the civil-law institution of delegation of authority, making the artifact legible to lawyers and auditors, not only to engineers. We give the mandate model and its decision semantics, the reference architecture as an MCP-transparent proxy with separated decision and enforcement points, and a mapping of the mechanism onto EU AI Act Articles 12 and 14, GDPR accountability, NIS2, and eIDAS 2, including a roadmap to qualified attestation through Qualified Trust Service Providers (QTSPs). We describe the implementation status of the reference system and a quantitative evaluation plan covering enforcement overhead, audit completeness, and tamper-evidence verification cost.
2608.14074.paper_summary_zh: AI 代理越來越多地通過標準化的工具調用協議（如模型上下文協議 MCP）對外部系統進行操作，但沒有基礎設施層限制其行為在主體可驗證授權的範圍內：授權邏輯存在於應用程式代碼中，既未簽名也無法獨立審計，所產生的日誌缺乏證據價值。我們提出了 Mandato，一種在協議層強制執行數位簽名授權的治理代理。授權是一種機器可讀的、經過加密簽名的授權工件，指定代理可以調用哪些工具、在什麼參數限制和上下文條件下、持續多長時間，以及代表誰；該代理根據適用的授權鏈評估每次工具調用，阻止不符合要求的調用，並在一個僅附加的、哈希鏈接的審計日誌中記錄每個決策——允許、拒絕，以及每個決策的證據——該日誌旨在用作證據，並通過合格的時間戳定期錨定。該授權故意以民法授權委託的制度為模型，使該工件對律師和審計師可讀，而不僅僅是對工程師。我們提供了授權模型及其決策語義、作為 MCP 透明代理的參考架構，並分離決策和執行點，還有該機制與歐盟 AI 法案第 12 條和第 14 條、GDPR 責任、NIS2 和 eIDAS 2 的對應關係，包括通過合格信任服務提供者（QTSP）獲得合格證明的路線圖。我們描述了參考系統的實施狀態和一個定量評估計劃，涵蓋執行開銷、審計完整性和防篡改證明成本。
2608.14074.author: Giovanni Racioppi et.al.
